page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Three viruses
steps.margin_note: Three named, with a fourth in reserve. Five lines.
lines: Three viruses with RNA as their genetic material:
Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) is a fourth.
steps.why: All four are common examples, so any three of them answer the question and the fourth is free insurance.
common_mistakes: Naming a bacteriophage. T-even phages have DNA, not RNA.
Naming only two. The question asks for THREE.
steps.memory_tip: Flu, polio, HIV — and TMV in plants.

steps.label: What that shows
steps.margin_note: One line on the significance, one on retroviruses.

lines.text: RNA can be genetic material too

lines: These viruses show that RNA can act as genetic
HIV and other retroviruses copy their RNA back
steps.why: RNA is thought to have been the first genetic material, which is why viruses that still use it are of more than passing interest.
common_mistakes: Saying only DNA can be genetic material. These viruses are the counter-example.
Leaving out the significance. Naming reverse transcriptase costs one line and adds real content.
steps.memory_tip: These are the exceptions to 'DNA is the genetic material'.
